# What this file does

This notebook checks that your R environment is set up correctly for the training. Run the chunks in order:

| Section | What it does |
|---|---|
| 1. Initial setup | Sets the CRAN mirror, install options and the editor packages (blocking) |
| 2. Rtools | Checks (or installs) the build toolchain needed by `mfbvar` and `nowcastDFM` |
| 3. CRAN packages | Installs the training packages available on CRAN |
| 4. GitHub packages | Installs `nowcastDFM` and `mfbvar` from source |
| 5. Libraries | Loads each package and reports it as OK, MISSING or BROKEN |
| 6. Smoke tests and summary | Fits each model on synthetic data and prints the final status |

**How to run it:** run each chunk in order with **▶ Run Cell** or `Ctrl+Enter`. The expected output is shown below each chunk. If something fails, read the note for that section before moving on. If you restart R at any point, run chunk 1 again first.

---

# If R does not start in VS Code: link the paths

If the terminal does not show the R prompt (`>`) and `R` is not recognized as a command, VS Code needs to be told where the R executables are. This happens when R was not added to the system PATH during installation.

**Recommended option: run Part 3 of the `act0_env_check.ipynb` notebook first.** That cell (Python kernel, it does not need R to start in VS Code) detects your R installation, writes the `r.rpath` / `r.rterm` keys to your `settings.json` and keeps a backup. Open the notebook, run the Part 3 cell, **close VS Code completely and reopen it**, then continue with this file.

**Manual option:** open an R session (for example from RGui) and run `R.home("bin")` to get the `bin` folder, something like `C:/Program Files/R/R-4.5.1/bin/x64`. Then in VS Code open the command palette with `Ctrl+Shift+P`, select **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)**, and add these two entries pointing to your path (adjust the version):

```json
"r.rpath.windows": "C:/Program Files/R/R-4.5.1/bin/x64/R.exe",
"r.rterm.windows": "C:/Program Files/R/R-4.5.1/bin/x64/Rterm.exe"
```

Save (`Ctrl+S`), close and reopen VS Code. R should now start.

> On macOS or Linux the keys are `r.rpath.mac` / `r.rterm.mac` and `r.rpath.linux` / `r.rterm.linux`, with the path returned by `R.home("bin")` on that system. The notebook detects the system and uses the right key automatically.

# Before you start: VS Code setup

**1. The R extension is installed.** Open the Extensions panel (`Ctrl+Shift+X`) and search for **"R"** by REditorSupport. It should show as installed and enabled.

**2. The `languageserver` popup.** When VS Code activates R, the extension may show a popup: *"The R package 'languageserver' is required to enable R language service features..."*. This is an editor package (autocomplete, signature help), not a training package. If it appears, click **"Yes"**. If you skip it or it never shows up, chunk 1 installs it anyway.

**3. The R terminal is active.** You should see the R prompt (`>`) in the VS Code terminal panel. If you see a regular shell prompt, run `R` in the terminal to start an R session.

---

# 1 · Initial setup

Run this chunk **before any other**: the rest of the notebook depends on it. It sets the CRAN mirror for this session and saves it to your `.Rprofile` for future sessions, sets install options (binaries first, parallel compilation), defines a fast package check and installs the editor packages (`jsonlite`, `languageserver` and `ps`). It is safe to run more than once.

> If R showed `vscode-R could not start the session watcher: there is no package called 'ps'` when it started, this chunk fixes it. After it installs the editor packages, restart the R terminal once (close it with the trash icon and open a new one), then run chunk 1 again and continue.

```{r setup}
# 1) CRAN mirror for the current session
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# 2) Save it to the user's .Rprofile (future sessions)
rprofile <- file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), ".Rprofile")
if (!(file.exists(rprofile) && any(grepl("repos", readLines(rprofile, warn = FALSE))))) {
  # Start on a new line if the file already has content, in case its last line
  # has no line break (otherwise the new line would be glued onto it)
  lead <- if (file.exists(rprofile) && file.size(rprofile) > 0) "\n" else ""
  cat(lead, 'options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))\n',
      file = rprofile, append = TRUE, sep = "")
  cat("Mirror added to .Rprofile:", rprofile, "\n")
} else {
  cat(".Rprofile already sets a mirror; left unchanged.\n")
}

# 3) Install options: prefer binaries (avoids compiling on Windows/macOS)
#    and compile in parallel when there is no other choice
options(install.packages.compile.from.source = "never",
        Ncpus = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))

# 4) Fast install check: does not load the package (requireNamespace does)
has_pkg <- function(p) nzchar(system.file(package = p))

# 5) Editor packages: languageserver (autocomplete, help), jsonlite and ps
#    (the session watcher that shows plots and the workspace in VS Code)
editor_pkgs <- c("jsonlite", "languageserver", "ps")
editor_missing <- editor_pkgs[!vapply(editor_pkgs, has_pkg, logical(1))]
if (length(editor_missing) > 0) {
  install.packages(editor_missing)
  cat("Editor packages installed. Restart the R terminal once so VS Code picks them up.\n")
}

cat("Initial setup done. Active mirror:", getOption("repos")[["CRAN"]], "\n")
```

**Expected output (first run):**
```
Mirror added to .Rprofile: C:/Users/user/Documents/.Rprofile
Initial setup done. Active mirror: https://cloud.r-project.org
```

# 2 · Rtools check

`mfbvar` and `nowcastDFM` are compiled from source, which requires Rtools45 (the Rtools version for R 4.5.x), a Windows build toolchain separate from R. This chunk checks whether it is installed and, if not, downloads and launches the official CRAN installer.

```{r rtools-check}
if (!has_pkg("pkgbuild")) install.packages("pkgbuild")

rtools_page <- "https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools45/rtools.html"

if (pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = FALSE)) {
  cat("Rtools OK: build tools found\n")
} else if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
  cat("Rtools NOT found. Downloading the Rtools45 installer from CRAN...\n")

  # The .exe name changes between builds, so it is read from the CRAN index
  files_dir <- "https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools45/files/"
  exe <- tryCatch({
    idx <- paste(readLines(files_dir, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
    hit <- regmatches(idx, regexpr("rtools45-[0-9]+-[0-9]+\\.exe", idx))
    if (length(hit) == 0) stop("installer not found in index")
    hit[1]
  }, error = function(e) NA_character_)

  # The installer is ~480 MB: R's default 60-second timeout is not enough
  options(timeout = max(1200, getOption("timeout")))

  dest <- if (!is.na(exe)) file.path(tempdir(), exe) else NA_character_
  ok <- !is.na(exe) && tryCatch({
    download.file(paste0(files_dir, exe), dest, mode = "wb")
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    unlink(dest)   # drop the partial file
    cat("Download failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    FALSE
  })

  if (ok) {
    # Silent install with default options; Windows only asks for admin permission (UAC)
    cat("Installing Rtools45 silently. Click 'Yes' on the Windows permission prompt\n",
        "and wait, this can take a few minutes...\n", sep = "")
    system2("powershell", c("-NoProfile", "-Command", shQuote(sprintf(
      "Start-Process '%s' -ArgumentList '/VERYSILENT','/SUPPRESSMSGBOXES','/NORESTART' -Verb RunAs -Wait",
      normalizePath(dest)), type = "cmd")))

    if (pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = FALSE)) {
      cat("Rtools OK: installed and detected\n")
    } else {
      cat("Install finished, but R does not detect Rtools yet.\n",
          "Restart R (or VS Code) and run chunks 1 and 2 again.\n", sep = "")
    }
  } else {
    cat("Could not download the installer automatically. Install it from:\n  ",
        rtools_page, "\n", sep = "")
    utils::browseURL(rtools_page)
  }
} else {
  cat("Rtools is Windows only. On macOS/Linux install the system build tools (Xcode Command Line Tools or build-essential).\n")
}
```

**Expected output:**
```
Rtools OK: build tools found
```

> If Rtools is missing, the chunk installs it silently with the default options: just accept the Windows permission prompt. If it then asks you to restart, restart R (or VS Code) and run chunks 1 and 2 again until you see `Rtools OK`. If the download fails, the chunk opens the Rtools page so you can install it from the browser. Rtools45 requires R 4.5.x; if your R is older, update it first.

# 3 · CRAN packages

Installs the CRAN packages that are not yet present. If everything is installed, it finishes in a second.

```{r install-cran}
cran_packages <- c("tidyverse", "lubridate", "openxlsx", "Rmisc",
                   "imputeTS", "midasr", "remotes", "knitr")

missing <- cran_packages[!vapply(cran_packages, has_pkg, logical(1))]
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  cat("Installing:", paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  install.packages(missing)
}

# Confirm the install worked (install.packages only warns on failure)
still_missing <- cran_packages[!vapply(cran_packages, has_pkg, logical(1))]
if (length(still_missing) == 0) {
  cat("All CRAN packages installed\n")
} else {
  cat("FAILED to install:", paste(still_missing, collapse = ", "),
      "\nRead the messages above and run this chunk again.\n")
}
```

# 4 · GitHub packages

`nowcastDFM` and `mfbvar` are not on CRAN: they are compiled from source on GitHub, which is why they need Rtools (section 2) and `remotes` (section 3). If one fails, the other still runs. `upgrade = "never"` skips the interactive prompt about updating other packages, so the install does not hang waiting for input.

> Compiling `mfbvar` can take several minutes. The chunk compiles its C++ files on several cores at once to speed this up. Let it finish before running the next chunk.

```{r install-github}
gh_packages <- c(nowcastDFM = "dhopp1/nowcastDFM", mfbvar = "ankargren/mfbvar")

# Compile each package's C++ files in parallel (Ncpus from chunk 1, capped at 4:
# every parallel compile of mfbvar's C++ code uses a lot of RAM)
Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = paste0("-j", min(getOption("Ncpus", 1L), 4L)))

for (p in names(gh_packages)) {
  if (has_pkg(p)) { cat(p, "is already installed\n"); next }
  cat("Installing", p, "from GitHub...\n")
  tryCatch(remotes::install_github(gh_packages[[p]], upgrade = "never"),
           error = function(e) cat("ERROR installing", p, ":", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
}

# Confirm the install worked
gh_missing <- names(gh_packages)[!vapply(names(gh_packages), has_pkg, logical(1))]
if (length(gh_missing) == 0) {
  cat("All GitHub packages installed\n")
} else {
  cat("FAILED to install:", paste(gh_missing, collapse = ", "),
      "\nCheck that chunk 2 shows 'Rtools OK' and run this chunk again.\n")
}
```

# 5 · Library check

Loads each package used in the training scripts, one by one, and reports whether it is `OK`, `MISSING` (not installed) or `BROKEN` (installed but fails to load, for example after an interrupted install). A failure does not stop the check, so you see the status of every package at once.

```{r libraries}
# Package -> what it is used for
required <- c(
  tidyverse  = "data manipulation and plots",
  lubridate  = "date arithmetic",
  openxlsx   = "Excel import/export (Session 2b)",
  Rmisc      = "CI(): confidence intervals for the BVAR prior",
  nowcastDFM = "dfm(), predict_dfm(): Dynamic Factor Model",
  imputeTS   = "na_mean(): missing value imputation",
  midasr     = "midas_r(), mls(): MIDAS regression",
  mfbvar     = "set_prior(), estimate_mfbvar(): MF-BVAR",
  jsonlite   = "JSON parsing utilities",
  remotes    = "installing packages from GitHub"
)

# Real check: actually load each package. remotes and jsonlite are only loaded,
# not attached, since the session does not need them.
check_pkg <- function(p) {
  if (!has_pkg(p)) return("MISSING")
  tryCatch({
    if (p %in% c("remotes", "jsonlite")) loadNamespace(p)
    else suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(p, character.only = TRUE))
    "OK"
  }, error = function(e) paste("BROKEN:", conditionMessage(e)))
}

lib_status <- vapply(names(required), check_pkg, character(1))
for (p in names(lib_status)) cat(sprintf("  %-11s %s\n", p, lib_status[[p]]))

libs_ok <- all(lib_status == "OK")
if (libs_ok) {
  cat("\nAll libraries loaded successfully\n")
} else {
  if (any(lib_status == "MISSING"))
    cat("\nMISSING: go back to sections 3 and 4.\n")
  if (any(startsWith(lib_status, "BROKEN")))
    cat("BROKEN: close VS Code and reinstall those packages from a fresh RGui session.\n")
}
```

**Expected output:**
```
  tidyverse   OK
  lubridate   OK
  ...
  remotes     OK

All libraries loaded successfully
```

> **Note on `jsonlite`:** in some VS Code setups a warning about `jsonlite` appears when R starts. It does not affect the training. Installing it explicitly (chunk 1) usually removes the warning; if it persists, ignore it.

# 6 · Smoke tests and summary

This chunk builds a synthetic dataset, fits the three models on it and prints the final summary. The goal is not an economically meaningful forecast, only to confirm that each estimation runs end to end on your machine. Each model runs independently: if one fails, the others still run and the error message is shown next to the failing model. When you run the chunk again after fixing a problem, models that already passed are skipped and only the failed ones run again. To force a full rerun, run `rm(smoke_cache)` first.

The data mimic Trinidad and Tobago's nowcasting setup: quarterly real GDP (`gdp_tto`) and two monthly indicators (`x1_tto`, `x2_tto`). All values are random; only the structure (frequencies, date range) replicates the real data.

```{r smoke-tests}
# ---- Synthetic data: 2010 Q1 to 2024 Q4 (60 quarters, 180 months) ----
set.seed(42)
dates_m <- seq(as.Date("2010-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 180)
gdp_tto <- cumsum(rnorm(60, mean = 0.4, sd = 1.2))            # quarterly GDP
factor  <- rep(gdp_tto, each = 3) + rnorm(180, sd = 0.5)      # shared factor
x1_tto  <- factor + rnorm(180, sd = 0.8)                      # e.g. tourist arrivals proxy
x2_tto  <- factor + rnorm(180, sd = 1.1)                      # e.g. exports proxy

# Cache of models that already passed in this session (reset with rm(smoke_cache))
if (!exists("smoke_cache")) smoke_cache <- c(MIDAS = NA_real_, BVAR = NA_real_, DFM = NA_real_)

# Runs one model, prints OK/FAILED and returns the forecast (NA if it fails).
# If the model already passed, it is skipped: expr is never evaluated.
run_smoke <- function(label, expr) {
  if (!is.na(smoke_cache[[label]])) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s OK (skipped, passed before), forecast: %.4f\n", label, smoke_cache[[label]]))
    return(smoke_cache[[label]])
  }
  out <- tryCatch({
    v <- as.numeric(expr)
    if (length(v) != 1 || !is.finite(v)) stop("model ran but did not return a valid forecast")
    v
  }, error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s FAILED: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(out)))
    NA_real_
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s OK, forecast: %.4f\n", label, out))
    smoke_cache[[label]] <<- out
    out
  }
}

cat("=== Smoke tests ===\n")
fcst <- c(
  # ---- MIDAS ----
  # mls(x, 0:3, 3) uses 4 monthly lags with ratio 3 = 12 monthly obs. consumed.
  # Quarters 5:60 for y and months 1:168 for x, so both have length 56.
  MIDAS = run_smoke("MIDAS", {
    y_midas <- gdp_tto[5:60]
    x_midas <- x1_tto[1:168]
    m <- midas_r(y_midas ~ mls(x_midas, 0:3, 3, nealmon),
                 start = list(x_midas = c(1, -0.5)))
    tail(fitted(m), 1)
  }),

  # ---- MF-BVAR ----
  # mfbvar takes ts objects: monthly series first, quarterly last
  BVAR = run_smoke("BVAR", {
    mf_list <- list(x1_tto  = ts(x1_tto,  start = c(2010, 1), frequency = 12),
                    x2_tto  = ts(x2_tto,  start = c(2010, 1), frequency = 12),
                    gdp_tto = ts(gdp_tto, start = c(2010, 1), frequency = 4))
    prior <- set_prior(Y = mf_list, n_lags = 3, n_reps = 50, block_exo = "gdp_tto")
    ci <- t(sapply(mf_list, function(s) CI(na.omit(as.numeric(s)), ci = 0.95)))
    moments <- interval_to_moments(ci[, c("upper", "lower")])
    prior <- update_prior(prior, d = "intercept",
                          prior_psi_mean  = moments$prior_psi_mean,
                          prior_psi_Omega = moments$prior_psi_Omega,
                          n_fcst = 4)
    m <- estimate_mfbvar(prior, prior = "minn", variance = "iw")
    predict(m, pred_bands = NULL) %>%
      dplyr::filter(variable == "gdp_tto") %>%
      dplyr::pull(fcst) %>%
      mean()
  }),

  # ---- DFM ----
  # nowcastDFM works at monthly frequency: quarterly GDP goes in the third month
  # of each quarter and is NA otherwise. nowcastDFM 1.0.0 expects monthly columns
  # first and quarterly last; otherwise it fails with "replacement has length zero".
  DFM = run_smoke("DFM", {
    df_dfm <- data.frame(
      date    = dates_m,
      x1_tto  = x1_tto,
      x2_tto  = x2_tto,
      gdp_tto = ifelse(month(dates_m) %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12),
                       rep(gdp_tto, each = 3), NA)
    )
    blocks <- data.frame(global = rep(1, ncol(df_dfm) - 1))   # single global factor
    m <- dfm(df_dfm, blocks = blocks, p = 1)
    tail(predict_dfm(df_dfm, m, months_ahead = 1, lag = 0)$gdp_tto, 1)
  })
)

# ---- Summary ----
# Rtools is checked directly, so the line is right even after an R restart.
# Libraries reuses chunk 5, which the models need in the same session anyway.
status <- c(Rtools    = pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = FALSE),
            Libraries = exists("libs_ok") && isTRUE(libs_ok),
            !is.na(fcst))

cat("\n=== Environment check summary ===\n",
    sprintf("  %-10s %s\n", names(status), ifelse(status, "OK", "FAILED")),
    "=================================\n", sep = "")
```

**Expected output:**
```
=== Smoke tests ===
  MIDAS  OK, forecast: [number]
  BVAR   OK, forecast: [number]
  DFM    OK, forecast: [number]

=== Environment check summary ===
  Rtools     OK
  Libraries  OK
  MIDAS      OK
  BVAR       OK
  DFM        OK
=================================
```

> If any line shows `FAILED`, read the error message printed next to that model and go back to the matching section. All five must show `OK` before starting the training exercises.
